data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental weather May 2029 trip means perfect spring conditions: average highs of 22°C, 10 hours of sunshine, and calm Mediterranean seas. This guide covers daily weather patterns, sea conditions, and practical tips to make your charter from Puerto Banús unforgettable. Whether you choose the Azimut 39 or the Mangusta 80, May offers ideal conditions for coastal cruising, swimming, and sunbathing.

Average Temperatures in May 2029

Daytime temperatures in Marbella average 22°C, with lows around 15°C after sunset. Sea temperatures reach 18-20°C, comfortable for swimming. The Sierra Blanca mountains shield the coast from northerly winds, keeping conditions stable. Pack a light jacket for evening returns to port.

Sunshine and UV Index

May delivers 10 hours of daily sunshine, with sunrises at 07:00 and sunsets near 21:30. UV index is moderate (6-7), so apply SPF 30+ sunscreen, wear a hat, and bring polarized sunglasses. Our boats have shaded areas on the flybridge or cockpit for breaks from direct sun.

Wind and Sea Conditions

Prevailing winds are light easterlies at 5-15 knots, creating gentle seas (0.5-1.5 m swell). The famous Poniente (west wind) occasionally picks up in the afternoon but rarely exceeds 20 knots. These conditions suit all boats in our Marbella boat rental fleet, from the compact Mariah SX21 to the 29m Ferretti 94.

Rainfall and Humidity

May is dry, with only 3-4 rainy days averaging 20 mm total. Humidity ranges 60-70%, feeling comfortable. Showers are brief and often occur overnight. The best charter windows are 10:00-18:00, when skies are clearest and seas calmest.

Best Boats for May Weather

For small groups, our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) at €749/2h are ideal. Larger parties should consider the Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h, includes jet ski) or the Azimut 58 Flybridge. All charters include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. For specific availability, book your May charter early.

Top Destinations in May

Head east to Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés for sheltered coves with calm water. Westbound trips to Cabopino and Estepona offer longer cruising. The Golden Mile coastline provides scenic views of La Concha mountain. May's light winds make these routes comfortable for all boat sizes.

Packing and Preparation Tips

Bring layers: a T-shirt, windbreaker, and sweater for evenings. Non-slip shoes are mandatory on deck. Our boats provide towels, but bring your own if preferred. Don't forget a waterproof phone case and a camera for dolphin sightings near Cabopino.
